tagline: Along Turnagain Arm's forty-foot tides, then over the Kenai to Seward.
intro: South out of Anchorage the highway comes down to Turnagain Arm and spends its first 50 miles between the Chugach Mountains and the water. The tides here can run to 40 feet, and the flood sometimes arrives as a bore, a single wave pushing up the arm. At low water the arm is a broad mud flat. Beluga whales travel it with the tides.

At the head of the arm the road turns into the Kenai Mountains, past Summit Lake and along Upper Trail Lake at Moose Pass, and comes down to Resurrection Bay. Until the highway was finished in 1951, Seward could be reached only by sea, rail or air.

moments.title: Turnagain Arm
moments.text: Captain Cook ran the Resolution aground on a sandbar here, found no Northwest Passage, and in a bad mood named the place River Turnagain.

moments.title: Portage
moments.text: The 1964 earthquake dropped the ground about six feet and put the town below high tide. A few ruins remain, with a ghost forest of trees killed by the salt water.

moments.title: Seward
moments.text: On the shore at the south end of town a marker shows Mile 0 of the original Iditarod Trail, and the Alaska Railroad comes to its end here too.
